extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for preparing, filing, formatting, and processing amendments, drawings, claims, fees, and submissions in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings under MPEP and the cited CFR/USC provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: All amendments made vis-à-vis patent being reexamined
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the patent being reexamined must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of the filing of reexamination. If there was a prior change to the patent (e.g., prior reexamination certificate, reissue, certificate of correction), the first amendment must be made relative to the patent specification as changed by the prior proceeding; all subsequent amendments must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the filing of the request for reexamination (and not relative to the prior amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reexamination certificate is printed, underlined matter is printed in italics and brackets printed as inserted in the proceeding to show additions/deletions. In rare instances where a concluded post-patent proceeding changes the patent while the reexamination is pending, amendments will be made relative to the patent as revised by the concluded proceeding and 37 CFR 1.530(i) is waived to that extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments after patent expiration (except cancellations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.530(j), no amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; if the patent expires during reexamination, all amendments to the claims and all claims added during the proceeding are withdrawn and canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out withdrawal by placing a diagonal line across all amended/new claims and text added to the specification in the amendment papers; notify patent owner in next Office action that amendments are improper and subsequent reexamination is on unamended patent claims. Examiner should ensure all rejected/objected claims are canceled and may issue examiner's amendment canceling such claims. Only cancellation of original patent claims is permitted in an expired patent; no amendments other than cancellation will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for specification amendments (presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending the specification, submit a copy of the entire paragraph being amended with underlining and bracketing to show the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Replace the paragraph beginning at [location] with the revised text and show insertions by underlining and deletions by brackets. Provide the full paragraph text with changes indicated, not only fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for claim amendments (presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes to patent claims, submit a copy of the entire patent claim with the amendments shown by underlining and bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dependency of an original claim is to be changed by amendment, it is proper to make that original patent claim dependent upon a later filed higher-numbered claim. Present the whole claim text with the changes from the original patent shown (underlines for additions, brackets for deletions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of entire claim(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: To cancel an original patent claim, provide an in-writing, direct cancellation of the entire claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: 'Claim 4. [canceled]' or 'Cancel claim 6.' Ensure cancellation is explicit in amendment papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims (format and numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim (a claim not found in the patent) should be presented with underlining throughout the claim. New claims are numbered beginning with the next higher number than the number of claims in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new claims added earlier are later canceled, examiners will renumber remaining new claims numerically at time of preparing NIRC so they follow the highest original claim number. A claim number previously assigned to a new claim that has been canceled should not be reassigned to a different new claim during the reexamination proceeding (e.g., if new claim 5 is canceled, a later new claim should be claim 6, not reuse 5). At NIRC issuance remaining new claims are renumbered for issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of new claims (must present entire amended text & support)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a new claim (a claim presented in the reexamination proceeding) must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material, and it must be underlined throughout the claim; the presentation cannot contain bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the amended claim does not indicate what changed from the previous version, the patent owner must point out what is changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment. Per 37 CFR 1.530(e), each change in the claim must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent (the reexamination specification) for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of original patent claims more than once (include prior and new changes correctly)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making more than one amendment to an original patent claim, the subsequent amendment must include both the changes previously presented in earlier amendments (as they relate to the original patent text) and the new changes being presented in the later amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletions introduced in a prior amendment that remove text not in the original patent should simply be omitted (not shown in brackets) in the subsequent amendment; words added earlier that are now deleted are omitted (not bracketed). Words that were added earlier and retained must be included in the later amendment if they came from the original amendment. Example shown with 'cutting means' → 'knife' → later change to 'serrated' demonstrates proper notation: the later amendment shows the claim text only relative to the original patent with additions underlined and deletions omitted where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendments must be submitted as new sheets; original drawings not altered
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Amendments to the original patent drawing sheets are not permitted; any change must be in the form of a new sheet of drawings for each drawing sheet that is changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon examiner approval of the sketch, file new sheets of drawings complying with 37 CFR 1.84. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' Do not mark the original patent drawing sheets; provide substitute/new sheets instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated Sheet and per-figure identifications on new drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing drawing changes, submit an 'Annotated Sheet' sketch as a separate paper for examiner approval. If a new drawing sheet contains multiple figures, each figure must be marked individually as 'Amended' or 'New' if applicable; it is insufficient to generally mark the entire sheet as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: new sheet contains Figures 1-3 but only Figure 2 is amended — the sheet must identify Figure 2 as 'Amended.' The 'Annotated Sheet' becomes part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: New drawing sheets must be entered before NIRC issuance; Quayle action if delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: New sheets of drawings must be entered into the reexamination record prior to preparation of a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC). If the proposed drawing correction is approved but the new sheets have not been filed and the proceeding is otherwise ready for NIRC, prepare an ex parte Quayle Office action setting a one-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for filing the new sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new sheets are not timely filed, the Reexamination Certificate will be issued with drawings that do not reflect the proposed changes/amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship via petition during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inventorship in the patent being reexamined must be corrected, a petition complying with 37 CFR 1.324 must be submitted during the prosecution of the reexamination proceeding; if granted, the reexamination certificate will include the amendment naming the actual inventor(s) and the certificate of correction is merged with the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reexamination concludes without issuance of a reexamination certificate (e.g., reexamination denied or order vacated), the patent owner may, after conclusion, request a certificate of correction indicating the change of inventorship. Alternatively, correction of inventive entity may be pursued by reissue under 35 U.S.C. 251 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees apply for claims added during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2) and 37 CFR 1.20(c) apply to excess claims proposed to be added to a patent during reexamination. The independent claims fee applies for each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent being reexamined; the total claims fee applies for each claim in excess of twenty and in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No excess claims fee is due if the amendment only revises existing claims without adding new claims. Examples illustrate combinations of canceled and added claims and when fees apply. Claims disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 or canceled via prior Reexamination Certificate, reissue patent, or Certificate of Correction are not counted in the patent for fee calculations. If fees are not paid when presenting excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) will set a one-month time period to correct the fee deficiency; failure to pay can result in termination of prosecution per 37 CFR 1.550(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fees for filing petitions in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(6), except for enumerated exceptions (e.g., petitions to extend period for response under 1.530(c), petitions to accept delayed response under 1.550(e), petitions under 1.78 for unintentionally delayed benefit claim, and petitions for correction of inventorship under 1.530(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amounts (as of cited revision): $1,940 for a large entity, $970 for a small entity, $485 for a micro entity (available for patent owners only). See 37 CFR 1.550(i) for scope of exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester reply timing and limits in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply by the ex parte reexamination requester to the patent owner's statement under § 1.530 may be filed within two months from the date of service of the patent owner's statement; the reply must be served on the patent owner. If the patent owner does not file a statement, no reply or other submission from the ex parte requester will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions of time are granted for this reply period (35 U.S.C. 304). The reply need not be limited to issues raised in the statement and may include additional prior art and raise any issue appropriate for reexamination. After filing the reply, the requester may not file any further papers; any further papers will be returned and not considered. The patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of the third party requester to circumvent the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of statements/replies — timeliness and proof of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve documents under §§ 1.530 or 1.535 may result in their being refused consideration; only the statement under 1.530 and the reply under 1.535 will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely submissions will ordinarily not be considered and will be returned to the sender (except untimely patent owner papers filed after the period set for response may be treated differently). Any paper requiring proof of service filed without proof may be denied consideration; Central Reexamination Unit should inquire about service if proof missing. See MPEP §§ 2266.03 and 2267 for service handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner consideration standards and scope of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served under §§ 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action. Examiner consideration of proposed amendments is guided by 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); consideration of the patent owner's statement is guided by 37 CFR 1.530(c); consideration of a third party reply is guided by 37 CFR 1.535.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the third party requester's reply raises issues not previously presented, the examiner will treat those issues in the Office action if they are within the scope of reexamination; issues outside the scope should be treated pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c). For handling of new matter, see MPEP § 2270.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination (general procedural rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the times for filing the statement and reply expire, reexamination is conducted according to procedures established for initial examination under sections 132 and 133 and will result in issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate. Reexamination proceedings are to be conducted with special dispatch within the Office. The patent owner may propose any amendment or new claim to distinguish the invention from cited prior art, but no amendment or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim will be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full search will not routinely be made by the examiner. After a third party requester files a request for ex parte reexamination, any document filed by either the patent owner or the requester must be served on the other party per § 1.248; lack of service may result in refusal of consideration. Reexamination proceeds even if notice to patent owner is returned undelivered (notice under 37 CFR 1.11(c) is constructive). Active participation by third party ends with the reply under § 1.535; no further submissions by requester will be acknowledged unless in accordance with §§ 1.510 or 1.535 or were entered prior to the order for reexamination under § 1.525.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions and handling delayed responses by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner in an ex parte reexamination will be given at least 30 days to respond to any Office action. Time for actions will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; requests for extension must be filed on or before the due date and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a response is not timely filed, delay may be excused if shown to be unavoidable (petition under 1.137(a)) or accepted if unintentional (petition under 1.137(b)). If patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response or required interview statement under § 1.560(b), prosecution will be a terminated prosecution and the Director will issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.570 per last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party submissions after order and limitations on filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Once ex parte reexamination is ordered, no further active participation by a third party requester is allowed, and no third party submissions will be acknowledged or considered unless they comply with § 1.510 or § 1.535 or were entered into the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination under § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may not file papers on behalf of the requester to circumvent ex parte rules. The Court held that a federal district court cannot order a patent owner to file papers prepared by a third party in addition to the owner's own submission; such papers will not be entered and filing them may render the entire submission an inappropriate response and be returned. Submissions by third parties filed after the order must meet requirements of § 1.501(a).
